evidence_class: measured on public owner-reported scores and on the public label raster; no organiser receipt and no private score
headline: Agreement with the public catalogue is ANTI-correlated with the reported public score. Any holdout built on labels.tif therefore ranks candidates backwards.

measurement_1_anti_correlation.instrument: blocked holdout, 5x4 blocks, 12 px guard, official DW-Tversky alpha=0.2 beta=0.8 R=300 m
measurement_1_anti_correlation.spearman_note: exactly monotone and decreasing over all four; combined with the earlier 32-submission rho = -0.79 this is a replicated finding, not a single-session artefact

measurement_2_ring_is_worthless.definition: mass fraction of the submission inside 200 m of data/labels.tif
measurement_2_ring_is_worthless.reading: monotone decreasing: ring mass earns no true-positive credit (the organiser masks known faults) but still pays the false-positive penalty, so it is pure loss
measurement_2_ring_is_worthless.independent_confirmation: owner record: pruning the 2,545 nearest-catalogue dots from a 40,199-dot submission moved the public score 0.2708 -> 0.2778

measurement_3_forward_model.derivation: with T + F ~= M (the kernels of distinct faults barely overlap) the official index reduces to DTI = T / (0.2 M + 0.8 G), where T is the weighted true-positive credit, M the total emitted mass and G the number of truth pixels
measurement_3_forward_model.reading: all four submissions have the SAME credit-per-unit-mass (0.0890 = 5.8x a random placement, but only 3% of the ideal 3.0 credit per dot for 600 m spacing). Their score differences are explained almost entirely by M and by ring mass, not by where inside the shell the dots fall

measurement_4_spacing.theory: a truth pixel takes max_x p(x) k(d), so two dots in one 300 m kernel do not add. For dots spaced s px along a line, credit per dot = s (1 - s/12), which plateaus at s = 6 px; s = 3 px already returns 2.25 of the ideal 3.0

measurement_5_marginal_rule.rule: add mass while the marginal credit per unit mass exceeds (0.2 M / (0.2 M + 0.8 G)) times the running average
measurement_5_marginal_rule.consequence: raising M above the incumbents' ~38k is profitable as long as the added dots are at least ~70% as good as the average; the candidate uses 43,038 dots

limitation: G and the credit-per-unit-mass were fitted from four owner-reported public scores on a model that assumes T + F = M. They are an inference, not an organiser receipt, and they describe the incumbents' predictor, not a new one
